- Model tends to overestimate prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes.
- Underestimates prices in the latter half of the forecast, particularly when the true price shows a downward trend or mean reversion.
- Overreacts to recent high values, leading to exaggerated overshoots in the immediate next period.
- Fails to capture mean reversion adequately — forecasts stay too high when prices are trending down.
- Shows persistent lag in adjusting to true price movements, especially in the 10–15 day window.
- Overconfident in short-term momentum, underestimating volatility or correction phases.
- When true price drops sharply after a peak, model often fails to recognize the correction and continues to forecast upward.
- Tends to underestimate the magnitude of price corrections following strong upward moves.
- Forecasts are overly smooth — fails to capture abrupt reversals or sudden drops in price.
- Overestimates the persistence of recent trends, especially in the 20–30 day window.
